rounds.text: Refractory Shapes Ltd is deeply under-appreciated because its exceptional multi-year growth profile is available at an exceptionally modest valuation of 12.6x P/E [E1] and 1.15x price-to-book [E2]. The company has compounded its sales at 22% [E8] and its profits at 24% [E11] over a five-year span, alongside an accelerated 36% profit growth over the last three years [E12] that outpaces the sector median profit growth of 21.8% [E60]. This disconnect between robust structural expansion and a stock sitting at just 2% of its 52-week range [E5] highlights a significant mispricing by the market. Conceded: [E4], [E7], [E13], [E55].

The bull highlights an attractive valuation of 12.6x P/E [E1] and 1.15x price-to-book [E2], but ignores that low valuations often trap capital when a business hits a wall, as evidenced by the stock sitting near the absolute bottom at just 2% of its 52-week range [E5]. While the bull leans on past 5-year sales growth of 22% [E8] and 3-year profit growth of 36% [E12], those historical metrics mask a sharp current contraction where trailing twelve-month profit growth has collapsed to -25% [E13]. Conceded: [E11]. Furthermore, the bull's optimism about earnings quality is directly contradicted by a mediocre return on equity of 9.6% [E7], a complete absence of shareholder returns with a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], and explicit screen warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E55].

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 1.15x (price ₹ 26.2 on a book value of ₹ 22.7).
The stock sits 2% of the way up its 52-week range (25 low to 66 high).
Compounded sales growth over 5 years is 22%.
Compounded profit growth over 5 years is 24%.
Compounded profit growth over 3 years is 36%.
Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months is -25%.
PRICE-LED — Recently, profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 26%, the company is starting to outperform expectations.
Screen reason (bear side): earnings growth decelerating
